articles.title: Ali G answers his critics: ‘Me ain’t the first intellectual to get haterz’
articles.summary: Staines’s finest nailed the zeitgeist of the late 90s and early 00s, and now he’s back – but how does he fit into 2026? He discusses the backlash against his return, his worst ever interviewee and how he’s going to prevent world war two.
body: “Can you tell people that you’re from Hustler?” Ali G asks me. “Or The Source. Or Guns & Ammo. Speaking to a Guardian journalist ain’t a good look for me in the hood.”

At Ali’s request, we are meeting in an independent chicken shop in Staines because – due to some sort of mix-up – he thought the one interview he had agreed to for his new film was Chicken Shop Date, which was “90% likely to lead to boning”. He follows this with an entirely unprintable reminiscence about the first time he and “me Julie” had sex in the disabled toilets of Egham KFC.

Now that we have established I am not in fact Amelia Dimoldenberg – and that any boning today will be strictly chicken-related – Ali changes tack. Whenever anyone comes near our table, he loudly explains, to my embarrassment, that we are actually conducting a major drug deal. Having seemingly worked his way through the entire menu, he starts asking what else he would need to buy to get the bill up to £500, after discovering that the Guardian is footing it.
points: Staines’s finest nailed the zeitgeist of the late 90s and early 00s, and now he’s back – but how does he fit into 2026?
He discusses the backlash against his return, his worst ever interviewee and how he’s going to prevent world war two.

Speaking to a Guardian journalist ain’t a good look for me in the hood.”

articles.title: Apichatpong Weerasethakul’s ‘Jengira’s Magnificent Dream,’ With Tilda Swinton, Boarded by ‘Triangle of Sadness’ Mexican Co-Producer Piano
articles.summary: Piano, the Mexican production and distribution company behind Ruben Östlund’s Palme d’Or-winning “Triangle of Sadness,” has boarded Apichatpong Weerasethakul’s “Jengira’s Magnificent Dream,” producer Julio Chavezmontes has confirmed. Tilda Swinton is attached to the project.
body: Joining Swinton are Thailand’s Jenjira Pongpas (“Cemetery of Splendor”) and Sakda Kaewbuadee (“Tropical Malady”) and Canadian actor Connor Jessup (“Falling Skies”).

In an interview with Variety, Chavezmontes discussed the company’s trajectory over the past 15 years while reflecting on its approach to identifying talent and developing co-productions. He stresses that the company remains open to projects across genres and formats, prioritizing a distinctive creative vision over mainstream formula.
“If something strikes us as potentially incredible, then the format is absolutely secondary,” he says.

Piano’s international outlook has been central to its growth, says Chavezmontes, whose many credits include Lucrecia Martel’s “Our Land,” Luis Ortega’s San Sebastian Horizons-winning “The Jockey” and Abel Ferrara’s ”Siberia.”

articles.title: NFL Introduces Celebrity Guest Cheerleaders: On the Sidelines With Comedian Atsuko Okatsuka and the L.A. Rams (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: It’s just before halftime of the Los Angeles Rams’ Monday Night Football matchup with the Buffalo Bills, and comedian Atsuko Okatsuka is standing in the tunnel, hyping herself up.
body: Okatsuka stops to share her instant reaction with Variety: “I’m so old,” she cracks.
A few minutes later, she sinks into a lounge chair in the green room to reflect on becoming the NFL ’s inaugural Celebrity Guest Cheerleader.
“The middle part I crushed,” Okatsuka says, beaming with pride. “It was so fun. It takes me back to performing good spirits through dance. I haven’t done that in a minute.”

The NFL’s Celebrity Guest Cheerleader initiative is the latest extension of the league’s successful “Celebrity Guest” series, which launched last year with pro athletes, actors and musicians — including Jerry Rice, Simone Biles, Suni Lee, Method Man, Common, Joel McHale, Ken Griffey Jr., Benson Boone and Marshawn Lynch — working as sideline photographers during games.

articles.title: Sergei Loznitsa’s ‘Imperium’ Wins Best Film at BFI London Film Festival
articles.summary: Sergei Loznitsa’s “Imperium,” which revisits the Soviet Union of the early 1970s through footage shot by Italian cameramen, has won the best film award at the 70th BFI London Film Festival competition. The prizes were unveiled Sunday as the festival drew to a close.
body: ‘9 Temples to Heaven,’ ‘Concrete Land’ and ‘Aman’ also take top prizes as the festival wraps its 70th edition.

In the first feature competition, the Sutherland Award went to Thailand’s Oscar submission “9 Temples to Heaven,” the first fiction feature from Sompot Chidgasornpongse. The film reflects on faith, kinship and the passage from life to death. Actor Amir El-Masry (“Giant,” “Limbo”) presided over that jury, joined by “Moonglow” producer Alemberg Ang and sales, distribution and awards strategist Rosa Bosch.
“An accomplished first feature paving his own path in the well-established tradition of filmmaking in the Southeast Asian region,” the jury said.

Bertil Nilsson’s “Masc” received a special mention in the same section. The debut tracks Robin, who drifts between short-term jobs and uncertain relationships while looking for somewhere he fits. The jury singled out Nilsson as a fresh British talent with an unusual concept and a funny script.

articles.title: James Austin Johnson’s Trump Stops by ‘SNL U.K.’ for Meeting With Burnham and Zelenskyy: ‘You Don’t Have One Guy Who Can Play Trump?’
articles.summary: Donald Trump made his first appearance on “SNL U.K.,” courtesy of “SNL” cast member James Austin Johnson. Saturday night’s cold open recreated U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham (George Fouracres) meeting with Ukraine’s President Zelenskyy (Freddie Meredith) to reaffirm Britain’s support in their war…
body: Johnson then appeared with his spot-on Trump impression, marking the first crossover between the “SNL U.K.” and “SNL” casts. “Did somebody say Richard E. Grant?” he said.

“That’s right, you say my name and I appear,” Johnson’s Trump sad. “I got the idea from my very close friend Beetlejuice, the late, great Beetlejuice. It’s one of the two ways I am like him, the other is sex pest — alleged, they can’t prove he did that stuff.”

When asked why he’s in the U.K., Johnson as Trump said he’s been in town “to see my favorite comedian” who is “performing live at high court in the role of defendant,” referencing the Russell Brand trial.

Johnson’s Trump then explained that he is hoping to do a job swap with Burnham. “I take over the U.K., you take over America,” he said. “I tell ya, that place is a real mess, you’re going to hate it. It’s an awful, awful job. It’s a terrible place full of disgusting people, I don’t know what the hell happened. C’mon, job swap with me!”

articles.title: Jesse Eisenberg Relives Kieran Culkin Woes Making ‘A Real Pain’ and Says His Next Project Is a TV Show
articles.summary: Producer Emma Stone had to chaperone Culkin on the plane to Poland because Eisenberg didn't know if he was going to show: "She sent me a video of him going through customs saying, 'We are here.'"
body: Jesse Eisenberg continues to tread the festival circuit with his musical comedy The Debut, and on Sunday afternoon was wildly entertaining at a high-energy Screen Talk event ahead of his film’s closing the BFI London Film Festival.

But there was one story in particular that had the room hanging onto Eisenberg’s every word, as he relived the chaotic process of working with Kieran Culkin on Eisenberg’s last film, A Real Pain — the same movie that would earn Culkin his first Oscar for best supporting actor last year.

“We didn’t know if Kieran was ever gonna show up to Poland,” began Eisenberg about the process ( A Real Pain stars him and Culkin as two Jewish-American cousins who reunite for a Holocaust heritage tour through Poland). “Kieran doesn’t call on anybody back — he’s one of those people that you hear about occasionally. They’re brilliant, but you don’t know if they’re gonna be there.”

articles.title: The Best-Dressed Stars at the Academy Museum Gala, Including Inde Navarrette and Taylor Swift
articles.summary: Taylor Swift in Dior, Sabrina Carpenter in Giorgio Armani Privé and Colman Domingo in custom Valentino were among the night's wow moments in style.
body: Forward-thinking style fresh from the Spring 2027 runways was mixed with archival and custom pieces among the stars who walked the red carpet at Saturday’s Academy Museum Gala — and if there was a common thread throughout many of the looks, it was a wonderful ease, an effortless blend of relaxed chic that’s not always present on an awards show carpet. After all, at the Academy Museum Gala, the few prizes awarded are predetermined and the pressure is off for everyone else.

An influential guest list gathering to celebrate their industry, but instead their shared love of cinema may ultimately be the reason the evening’s overall style blends the aforementioned relaxed-chic aesthetic with a splash of drama and, in many cases, an undeniable sense of fun. Each is found in the 15 looks that topped our list.

articles.title: Are Starfleet Officers Allowed To Date On Star Trek?
articles.summary: We've seen several Star Trek episodes involving romantic relationships, but what do Starfleet's official rules say about fraternization? Let's explore.
body: Welcome to Trekspertise, a series where we break down the technology, history, details, and decisions that make the Star Trek universe so complex — and so fun.

There are many episodes throughout the "Star Trek" franchise wherein Starfleet officers merrily fraternize. One might immediately recall the "Star Trek: The Next Generation" episode "The Naked Now," in which Tasha Yar (Denise Crosby) became infected with an intoxicating virus and seduced Data (Brent Spiner). Or the episode "In Theory," wherein Data began an experimental romance with officer Jenna D'Sora (Michele Scarabelli).

"Star Trek" has also been full of full-blown marriages. Commander Riker (Jonathan Frakes) married Counselor Troi (Marina Sirtis) on in the "Next Generation" movies. On "Star Trek: Deep Space Nine," Worf (Michael Dorn) married Jadzia Dax (Terry Farrell), which, incidentally, proved to be easy character development for the actors because the romance didn't have to be forced. Furthermore, on "Star Trek: Voyager," Tom Paris (Robert Duncan McNeill) married B'Elanna Torres (Roxann Dawson).
points: We've seen several Star Trek episodes involving romantic relationships, but what do Starfleet's official rules say about fraternization?

articles.title: ‘Imperium,’ ‘Concrete Land’ and ‘9 Temples to Heaven’ Win BFI London Film Festival Awards
articles.summary: 'Aman' was honored in the short film competition, while LFF special mentions went to 'Queer Edward II,' 'MASC' and 'Daughters of the Late Colonel'
body: The 70th edition of the BFI London Film Festival (LFF) is wrapping up Sunday night with the U.K. premiere of Jesse Eisenberg ’s star-studded The Debut, following the afternoon unveiling of this year’s award winners. The 2026 honors were led by Sergei Loznitsa ‘s Imperium, which won the best film award in the official competition, and Asmahan Bkerat’s Concrete Land, which was named the winner of the Grierson Award in the LFF documentary competition.

“ Imperium is an extraordinary film that explores the Soviet Union in the early 1970s from a rich archive with a wide-ranging perspective that looks at life in a country with an extraordinary social and cultural landscape that has rarely been seen,” the LFF jury said. “The film is richly evocative and emotionally engaging on all levels, giving us a visually arresting perspective of life before the Soviet Union was broken apart.”

Palestinian-Jordanian director Bkerat’s Concrete Land tells the story of a Palestinian Bedouin family displaced in Jordan. The young filmmaker told THR in a recent interview that the family featured in the film helped her discover her love for documentary filmmaking.
points: 'Aman' was honored in the short film competition, while LFF special mentions went to 'Queer Edward II,' 'MASC' and 'Daughters of the Late Colonel'

articles.title: TV Icon Lee Majors Was In A Star-Studded Comedy That Notoriously Flopped At The Box Office
articles.summary: Lee Majors is a well-known TV star, but he's made some movies, too - including this star-studded comedy that flopped hard at the box office.
body: Lee Majors will forever be known as the Six Million Dollar Man and the original Fall Guy. But his career stretched far beyond those hit 1970s and '80s series, and Majors worked hard to prove he was more than his best-known roles. When it comes to Bob Odenkirk's 2007 comedy "The Brothers Solomon," however, he'd probably prefer you to focus on his two beloved TV shows.

In 2007, Odenkirk was two years away from making his debut as Saul Goodman on "Breaking Bad," and had recently been beaten to the role of Michael Scott on "The Office" by Steve Carell. In the interim, he made a couple of movies that didn't fare too well with critics or audiences. 2006's "Let's Go to Prison" starred Dax Shepard, Will Arnett, and Chi McBride and earned a lowly 13% critic score on Rotten Tomatoes. In 2007 Odenkirk re-teamed with Arnett and McBride for "The Brothers Solomon." But this time he brought Lee Majors along. Unfortunately, it didn't help.
points: Lee Majors is a well-known TV star, but he's made some movies, too - including this star-studded comedy that flopped hard at the box office.

articles.title: ‘What Belongs to Others’ Wins Top Warsaw Film Festival Award
articles.summary: Cai Chengjie was named best director for 'Suzhou Quartet,' while 'Agia' was honored with the Competition 1-2 award at the 42nd edition of the Polish festival.
body: The 42nd edition of the Warsaw International Film Festival is wrapping up on Sunday after its winners were unveiled during a Saturday night awards ceremony. The top honor, the Warsaw Grand Prix in the international competition of the Polish fest, went to Grzegorz Dębowski for What Belongs to Others.

The Warsaw best director award went to Chinese filmmaker Cai Chengjie for Suzhou Quartet, which the jury lauded as “an original and ambitious concept brought to life through striking cinematography and daring experimentation with narrative form.” The “visually captivating and richly layered meditation on life and mortality” tells the story of four people who meet by chance in a small noodle shop, only to find they are long-lost acquaintances.

The jury lauded the actress for “a remarkably precise and emotionally truthful portrayal [and] for creating a complex character with great sensitivity and without exaggeration.” It added that the honor is also “for a role that stays with the audience long after the film ends.”
points: Cai Chengjie was named best director for 'Suzhou Quartet,' while 'Agia' was honored with the Competition 1-2 award at the 42nd edition of the Polish festival.
